findings.summary: gitea_api() got --max-time 60/1800, but gh_api() has no timeout bound at all (no --max-time or --connect-timeout). The brief says 'bound how long any single request can run' without scoping that to only the Gitea helper. gh_api is called in the enumeration/pagination loop that runs before the batch loop even starts, so a stalled connection to api.github.com (common failure mode: TCP connect succeeds, server never responds) hangs the entire nightly cron run indefinitely — exactly the failure mode the brief was written to close.

findings.summary: Implementer report claims 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff touches only this one script — no test file was added or modified. The repo has an established convention for exactly this (scripts/tests/deploy-pull.test.sh sources the script, stubs external commands like docker, and asserts on function-level behavior), and no gitea-mirror-github test exists anywhere in the repo. This task is specifically about a subtle bash correctness property (status surviving a command-substitution subshell boundary) — the kind of bug a source-and-stub test would catch directly — and it shipped with zero automated verification despite the report's claim to the contrary. Note the script also has no main-guard, so it isn't currently structured to be sourced for such a test without a small refactor.
